watchlist.name: Air Liquide
watchlist.blurb: Air Liquide closed at €191.96 in Paris on Friday, up 0.9% from Thursday's €190.32 close, as European shares rallied with Wall Street's Black Friday rebound. At the ECB's Nov 27 reference rate of 1.0957 the quote converts to $210.33, just under the year's high of €194.70. Industrial-gas demand stays steady and the CAC 40 is firm; the next Paris session sets the following print.

watchlist.name: Anthropic
watchlist.blurb: Anthropic surged 11.0% to $91.88 in Friday's short session, well above its $83 IPO price, as beaten-down AI names bounced after Wednesday's rout. The stock has now climbed sharply from its $82.79 Wednesday close, leading the AI rebound. The Nov 20 Navier-Stokes blow-up claim with NYU's Tristan Buckmaster is still unverified, its numerical certificate unreleased — watch for that proof to land or fade.

watchlist.name: SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Mo T-Bill
watchlist.blurb: BIL edged up to $91.67 as the short session ended, its distribution yield holding at 4.04% after the $0.30849 payout ex Nov 2 and paid Nov 5. The T-bill ETF keeps grinding a few cents higher each session while the Fed looks all but certain to hike on Dec 9, keeping short rates elevated. Nothing flashy, which is the point — it is the portfolio's cash anchor while AI names whip around.

watchlist.name: Alphabet
watchlist.blurb: Alphabet rose 0.7% to $274.96 in Friday's rebound, a modest gain after Wednesday's AI selloff cut the Nasdaq sharply. The stock remains well below its autumn highs as investors weigh tariff proposals aimed at Asian tech supply chains. Google's cloud and AI momentum still underpin the story; watch whether Monday's full session extends the bounce or the tariff worries return.

watchlist.name: Eli Lilly
watchlist.blurb: Eli Lilly was nearly flat at $1,392.38, up a fraction in Friday's broad rally, holding near record territory. The drugmaker's weight-loss and diabetes franchises keep driving the valuation, with investors watching prescription data and pipeline news. Lilly has been one of the steadier big-cap names through the week's AI-driven swings; the next catalyst is likely clinical or pricing news.

watchlist.name: Cheniere Energy
watchlist.blurb: Cheniere rose 1.0% to $305.04 as energy names joined Friday's rally and natural gas markets stayed firm into winter. LNG export demand remains the long-term driver, with Gulf Coast terminals running hard and new capacity coming. The stock sits near its highs; watch Henry Hub prices and any fresh contracting news for the next leg, plus how the Strait of Hormuz disruption affects global gas flows.

watchlist.name: Nvidia
watchlist.blurb: Nvidia gained 0.8% to $150.49 in Friday's AI rebound, a quieter day after Wednesday's rout and Monday's surge on Jensen Huang's reinstatement. The stock is still far below its highs as the board's independent investigation and the SEC probe continue, with Huang's Dec 1 House appearance ahead. Sean's call stands: long-term hold until the probes shake out — updates only on smoking guns, not noise.

watchlist.name: Pfizer
watchlist.blurb: Pfizer ticked up 0.2% to $28.52, barely moving in Friday's broad rally as the drugmaker continues its slow grind. The dividend remains the main attraction while investors wait for pipeline readouts to revive growth. Pfizer has lagged the market's AI-led swings in both directions; the next move likely needs a clinical win or a capital-return announcement rather than tape momentum.

watchlist.name: Rocket Lab
watchlist.blurb: Rocket Lab jumped 8.2% to $50.88, leading Friday's rebound as space names rallied with the broader market. The move extends a strong run for the small launcher, with investors focused on launch cadence and the Neutron program's progress. Starship's 15th flight is also in the air this weekend, keeping space in the headlines; watch for fresh launch or contract news to sustain the momentum.

watchlist.name: Rithm Capital
watchlist.blurb: Rithm Capital rose 0.9% to $9.00 in Friday's rally, continuing its steady climb toward the $9 level. The mortgage REIT's double-digit dividend yield keeps income buyers interested while rates stay high, and a near-certain December Fed hike could reshape the mortgage market for originators and servicers alike. Watch the Fed's Dec 9 decision and any update on Rithm's origination and servicing volumes.

watchlist.name: SpaceX
watchlist.blurb: SpaceX climbed 4.8% to $133.59 as space and AI names rebounded on Black Friday. Starship's 15th flight is two weeks past: Ship 42 reached orbit Nov 13 and was caught by the Starbase tower Nov 14 — a first — though Booster 22 was lost in the Gulf. Next is Flight 16, targeted no earlier than December with Booster 23 and Ship 43, possibly the first Starship launch from Florida's LC-39A. Watch for a firm date.

watchlist.name: Truist Financial
watchlist.blurb: Truist rose 1.3% to $48.50 in Friday's broad rally, tracking the banks higher as the market recovered. The lender benefits from a steepening curve and steady credit, though a December Fed hike is now nearly fully priced. Watch Monday's full session and any fresh economic data for direction; Truist's next company-specific catalyst is likely its investor day or quarterly update.

watchlist.name: U.S. Antimony
watchlist.blurb: U.S. Antimony rose 2.3% to $2.26 in Friday's rebound, bouncing with the small-cap miners after Wednesday's selloff. Antimony remains a critical-mineral story tied to defense demand and China export curbs, with UAMY's domestic supply position the long-term bull case. The stock is still near its lows; watch for fresh DOD or critical-mineral policy news to spark the next leg.

watchlist.name: Uranium Energy
watchlist.blurb: Uranium Energy jumped 5.1% to $5.98 as uranium names joined Friday's rally, with the sector still drawing buyers on the nuclear-expansion story. Term uranium prices sit near record levels and U.S. reactor restarts keep the demand case alive. UEC remains a long-term holding at these levels; watch for fresh utility contracting announcements or government uranium-buying news.

watchlist.name: VI5TC (est.)
watchlist.blurb: VI5TC's estimate rose 1.6% to $150.00, tracking the S&P 500's Black Friday rally to 7,297.49 in the shortened session. The S&P-anchored estimate moves with the index, and Friday's gain capped the market's best week since April 2025. The estimate refreshes with each index close; watch Monday's full session to see whether the rally holds into December after the holiday-shortened week.

watchlist.name: Valero Energy
watchlist.blurb: Valero gained 2.0% to $329.39 as refiners rallied with oil's weekly gain, though Brent eased Friday to $94.22 on the front-month contract. The Jazan refinery attack and Hormuz tanker incidents keep a risk premium in crude, supporting refining margins. Valero sits near its highs; watch OPEC+'s Sunday meeting on 2027 output and any fresh Gulf disruption for the next move.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Target 2035
watchlist.blurb: Vanguard Target 2035 held at $28.45, its Nov 25 net asset value, with Friday's NAV not yet published at build time. The target-date fund keeps its glide path toward a 2035 retirement, blending stocks and bonds that shift more conservative each year. It barely notices single-day tape swings; the next print comes with Monday's close, and the fund's mix does the work quietly.

watchlist.name: Schwab Value Advantage MF
watchlist.blurb: SWVXX holds its $1.00 NAV, with Schwab's 7-day SEC yield at 3.79% as published Nov 25, unchanged from the prior reading. The sweep fund keeps doing its quiet job while the market whipsaws — the VIX is still above 23 after spiking to 28.29 Wednesday. Per the standing plan, balances above $1,000 get swept into CDs, so the position should keep shrinking steadily toward zero.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Treasury MMF
watchlist.blurb: VUSXX holds its $1.00 NAV, with Vanguard's 7-day SEC yield at 4.01% as published Nov 25, unchanged from the prior reading. The Treasury money fund remains the eTrade cash vehicle, earning more than Schwab's SWVXX while the Fed looks set to hike again on Dec 9, lifting money-market yields further. It is the parking spot for sale proceeds, including the eventual Seiver Slough and Lodge sales.

breaking.headline: Wall Street caps best week since April with Black Friday rally
breaking.fact: The S&P 500 closed up 1.6% at 7,297.49, the Nasdaq 2.3% at 24,129.50 and the Dow 1.2% at 50,774.94 in Friday's shortened session, capping the market's best week since April 2025 as investors bought back beaten-down AI shares after Wednesday's rout; Nvidia joined the rebound, up 0.8%.

breaking.headline: OPEC+ set to hold output steady into early 2027
breaking.fact: OPEC+ producers have agreed in principle to keep first-quarter 2027 output targets unchanged at Sunday's meeting, three sources told Reuters, with the Iran war and disputes over capacity estimates clouding the talks; Rystad sees a global surplus of about 5 million barrels a day next year even if Gulf supplies only partly recover.

breaking.headline: Texas bids to bring U.S. Space Academy to Houston
breaking.fact: Texas has formally proposed Houston — alongside NASA's Johnson Space Center — as home of the new United States Space Academy, with groundbreaking targeted by 2027 and the first 300 students in 2028; Sens. Ted Cruz and senator-elect James Talarico jointly endorsed the bid this week.

breaking.headline: Fed hike in December now a near-certainty after hot inflation data
breaking.fact: CME FedWatch put the odds of a quarter-point Fed hike on Dec 9 at 98.6% on Friday morning after October PCE inflation printed 3.8% and third-quarter GDP was revised up to 4.3%; a hike would lift the policy rate and shape CD and money-market yields into 2027.

weekInBrief.headline: U.S.-led group agrees to buy Lukoil's overseas empire in share swap
weekInBrief.body: A consortium led by Todd Boehly's Eldridge, including the U.S. International Development Finance Corp., agreed to acquire Lukoil International — oil fields in 11 countries, three European refineries and 2,000 gas stations — from sanctioned Russian parent Lukoil. The deal is a share swap, so no cash goes to Russia, and the U.S. government gets an equity stake via the DFC; it still needs U.S. Treasury OFAC approval.

weekInBrief.headline: ECB minutes point to a December hike as inflation runs at 4%
weekInBrief.body: The account of the ECB's October meeting, published Nov 26, showed a large number of Governing Council members could have backed a hike then, and markets now price a 94.4% chance of a 25-basis-point rise on Dec 17, which would lift the deposit rate to 2.75%. Eurozone inflation hit 4.0% in October; EU leaders also endorsed Pablo Hernández de Cos to succeed Christine Lagarde as ECB president in February.

weekInBrief.headline: Bank of Korea hikes again as the AI chip boom powers growth
weekInBrief.body: South Korea's central bank raised its benchmark rate a quarter point to 3.25% on Thursday, its third hike since July, as semiconductor exports boom and inflation stays elevated. The bank also lifted its growth forecasts to 3.9% for 2026 and 4.1% for 2027; two of the seven board members voted to hold.

weekInBrief.headline: Bitcoin ETFs suffer their worst month on record
weekInBrief.body: U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs have lost a net $5.39 billion in November through Nov 25, already the largest monthly outflow since the funds launched in January 2024, beating June's $4.51 billion record. BlackRock's IBIT accounts for about $4.5 billion of the redemptions, and bitcoin is down about 22% this month to near $60,000.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said a projectile struck Aramco's Jazan refinery on Thursday, killing a Nepalese worker and wounding several others and temporarily halting part of the 400,000-barrel-a-day plant; the Saudi-led coalition blamed Yemen's Houthis, a day after they claimed a strike on the Ras Tanura refinery, and said it hit 50 targets in Yemen. The IRGC said two tankers exploded and caught fire after striking mines north of Oman's Khasab port, one a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels, and UKMTO reported a projectile striking a tanker off Oman on Wednesday. Iran's navy claimed it recovered two tankers seized by U.S. forces, the EU's von der Leyen called for more pressure on Iran, and President Trump said “victory” is at hand.

space.headline: Starship Flight 16 is next: December target, Florida debut possible
space.body: Two weeks after Flight 15 made history — Ship 42 caught by the Starbase tower on Nov 14 after a 22-hour orbital flight, while Booster 22 was lost in the Gulf — attention has shifted to Flight 16. It pairs Booster 23 with Ship 43, is targeted no earlier than December, and could be the first Starship launch from Kennedy's LC-39A. SpaceX has not announced a firm date, and no launch license had been announced as of mid-November.

space.headline: Deepest explosive eruption ever found, 4 miles down in the Mariana Trench
space.body: Marine geologists using the remotely operated vehicle Jason/Medea found pyroclastic rocks — telltale debris of an explosive eruption — on the walls of the Mariana Trench near Challenger Deep, about 6,500 meters down, the deepest-known explosive volcanic eruption on Earth. The rocks show recent igneous activity in a place long assumed too deep and too pressured for explosive eruptions; the findings appear in Frontiers in Earth Science.

space.headline: Internet cables map New Zealand's Alpine Fault in unprecedented detail
space.body: Researchers turned a 30-kilometer strand of dark fiber-optic cable along New Zealand's Haast Pass into thousands of seismic sensors and captured the sharpest view yet of the Alpine Fault's interior. The fault is not a single break but a roughly 200-meter-wide zone of shattered rock with up to six narrow slip cores, and the main core runs continuously for about 180 kilometers — evidence the fault's segments stay connected at earthquake depths. The work appears in Science Advances.

space.headline: The faintest supernova ever seen refuses to fade
space.body: Astronomers using the BlackGEM telescopes in Chile found the faintest supernova observed to date, SN 2024vjm in the galaxy NGC 6744 about 30 million light-years away, and it has stayed visible for nearly a year. It likely came from a white dwarf and a small companion star, and the odd, dim, long-lived explosion may reshape ideas about binary-star evolution and how supernovae are used to measure the universe's expansion. The results appear in Nature Astronomy.

apod.credit: NASA — NASA Image of the Day, Nov. 27, 2026
apod.explanation: NASA astronaut Andre Douglas, Artemis III mission specialist, stands inside an RS-25 engine test article during a visit to the Vehicle Assembly Building at Kennedy Space Center, where the agency is preparing the Artemis III mission to return astronauts to the Moon.
